summary: Uummannaq Heliport (UMD) is a vital Arctic transportation hub serving the small town of Uummannaq on an island in western Greenland, about 600 km north of the Arctic Circle. The heliport is the primary link connecting this remote settlement of roughly 1,500 residents to the broader Greenlandic aviation network, as no road connections exist between towns in this region. Set against the dramatic backdrop of the 1,170-meter Uummannaq Mountain, the heliport is operated by Air Greenland and handles scheduled flights as well as medical and charter services.
faqs:
Q: Who operates flights at Uummannaq Heliport?
A: Air Greenland operates scheduled helicopter services from this heliport, connecting Uummannaq to Ilulissat and other regional destinations.

Q: Is Uummannaq Heliport used for emergency medical services?
A: Yes, the heliport handles medevac flights and is essential for transporting patients to larger medical facilities in Ilulissat or Nuuk.

Q: When is the heliport operational?
A: Helicopter flights generally operate year-round, though schedules may be affected by severe Arctic weather conditions such as storms and heavy snowfall.

Q: Are there roads connecting Uummannaq to other towns?
A: No, there are no roads between towns in this part of Greenland. Helicopters and boats are the only ways to travel between Uummannaq and neighboring settlements.
transport_tips: The heliport is located a short distance from the town center, easily reached on foot in a few minutes. There is no public bus service, so passengers typically walk or arrange a pickup with their hotel or guesthouse. Arriving passengers should be prepared for variable weather and allow extra time during winter months when snow and ice can affect walking conditions.
local_tip: Book helicopter tickets well in advance during peak tourist season (June through August) and around the winter Northern Lights season, as seats are limited and the helicopter is the only quick way in or out of town.
